title: Awinyn, loghyn as y keayn
description: Ten short stories about rivers, lakes and the sea: a walk down a river glen to an inlet full of plovers, rock pools at low tide, a harbour café that swaps pineapple for quince jam, a river flood and a pregnant cow, a dragon boat race on a lake, a tidal turbine, an old abbey by a river, a campaign to save a river from a factory, a pharmacist and an audiobook about a great river, and divers who find a wartime plane in the sea.

lessons.title: Cosheeaght rish yn awin
lessons.summary: The sociologist Sioned Trewin, who studies how people live together in small villages, takes a casual walk down a river glen with her fisherman friend Euros Macrae; they hear and then see a woodpecker, eat bilberries that turn their tongues blue, and reach a small inlet where plovers run on the sand, and Euros tells her an old saying about plovers and winter, which she writes down.
lessons.text:
Ta Sioned Trewin ny sheshoayllee ec yn ollooscoill ayns Doolish. T'ee jannoo studeyrys er sleih, er nyn mooinjerys as er yn aght t'ad cummal cooidjagh ayns balley beg. Ta'n obbyr eck scanshoil, agh ta feme eck er tammylt ersooyl veih lioaryn as veih co-earrooderyn. Er-y-fa shen, Jesarn shoh chaie, hie ee er cosheeaght lesh e carrey Euros Macrae.

Cha nel Euros ny sheshoayllee. She eeasteyr eh, as t'eh er ve cummal rish yn awin ayns y glion ny slane vea. Ta enney echey er ny eeastyn awinagh, as er dy chooilley chreg as dy chooilley villey er y raad.

“Bee shoh cosheeaght neuchooishagh,” dooyrt Euros. “Cha nel shin goll dy loayrt mychione obbyr. Ta shin goll dy akin ushagyn as dy ee bee mooie.”

Hie ad sheese rish yn awin veih ny sleityn. Va'n ushtey glen as feayr, as va ram lossreeyn awinagh gaase er y vroogh. Hoshiaght, va'n raad eddyr biljyn mooarey. Dy gerrid, cheayll ad sheean jeh fuygh. “Snoggeyder t'ayn,” dooyrt Euros. “T'eh bwoalley e ghob noi'n billey dy gheddyn beishteigyn.” Lurg tammylt, honnick ad y snoggeyder hene, ushag ghlass lesh kione jiarg.

Faggys da'n raad, va tom beg lane dy vessyn gorrym. “Freoghane,” dooyrt Euros. “Ta ny freoghane mie dy ee, agh ta'n chengey ayd goll gorrym.” Ren ad ny freoghane y ee, as ren Sioned gearey tra honnick ee yn chengey gorrym ec Euros.

Ec y jerrey, haink ad dys branlaig veg, raad ta'n awin roie stiagh 'sy keayn. Va ushagyn lheamyssagh er geinnagh ny branlaig: ushagyn marrey, kiarkyn ushtey as feddagyn beggey. Ta ny feddagyn roie dy tappee er y gheinnagh, as t'ad shassoo dy doaltattym. “T'ad shirrey bee 'sy gheinnagh fliugh,” dooyrt Euros. “Ta shennockle ain: tra ta ny feddagyn çheet dys traie ny branlaig, ta'n gheurey çheet neesht.”

Ren Sioned screeu yn shennockle ayns e lioar veg. “S'mie lhiam yn shennockle shen,” dooyrt ee. “Ta cliaghtaghyn lheamyssagh ec sleih lheamyssagh, as ta shennockle er lheh ec dy chooilley valley.”

Ren ad shibbyr y ee er creg faggys da'n ushtey, as eisht hie ad thie er raad elley. Va Sioned scuirrit, agh v'ee maynrey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr t'ec Sioned Trewin?
She sheshoayllee ee ec yn ollooscoill ayns Doolish.
Row cosheeaght neuchooishagh oc?
Va. Va cosheeaght neuchooishagh oc, gyn loayrt mychione obbyr.
Cre honnick ad eddyr ny biljyn?
Honnick ad snoggeyder, ushag ghlass lesh kione jiarg.
Cre'n daah va er ny freoghane?
Va ny freoghane gorrym.
Cre va roie er geinnagh ny branlaig?
Va feddagyn beggey roie er y gheinnagh.
Cre'n shennockle ta ec Euros?
Tra ta ny feddagyn çheet dys traie ny branlaig, ta'n gheurey çheet neesht.

lessons.title: Ny askaidyn marrey
lessons.summary: The primary teacher Delyth Tulloch takes her class to the rock pools in Peel at low tide, where two clever ten-year-olds, Mabon and Llinos, find sea anemones with tube-shaped bodies, a hermit crab carrying an anemone in a partnership that helps both, the empty shell of a crab that has grown out of it with its claws intact, and grains of every colour in the sand.
lessons.text:
Ta Delyth Tulloch ny ynseyder ayns scoill vunnee ayns Pheeil. Un voghrey 'sy tourey, ghow ee e brastyl sheese dys ny creggyn rish y traie. Va'n keayn thannaghey, as dagh minnid va'n ushtey ny s'inshley. “Tra ta'n ushtey thannaghey,” dooyrt Delyth, “ta poyll beg faagit eddyr dagh chreg, as ta ram cretooryn bio ayns dagh poyll.”

Va Mabon as Llinos, daa phaitçhey jeih bleeaney d'eash, roie hoshiaght. Ta Mabon feer tushtagh, as t'eh shirrey fys mychione dy chooilley nhee. Ta Llinos tushtagh neesht, agh cha nel ee loayrt mennick.

Ayns y chied poyll, honnick ad ram meeryn jiarg as bog er y chreg. “Cre t'ad?” dooyrt Llinos. “Askaidyn marrey,” dooyrt Delyth. “Ta corp rollianagh ec dagh askaid, myr piob veg. Tra ta'n ushtey harrish, t'ee fosley as cur magh snaieyn beggey dy ghlackey bee. Tra ta'n keayn thannaghey, t'ee dooney as t'ee jeeaghyn myr meer dy hassoo jiarg.” Va Mabon gearey. “She askaid ta ec my vraar er e wannal!” “Shen y fa,” dooyrt Delyth. “Ta'n fockle askaid ny ennym er meer jiarg er y chrackan neesht.”

'Sy nah poyll, va partan beg cummal ayns shlig shenn. Er y shlig, va askaid veg. “Ta shimbosh ayn,” dooyrt Delyth. “Ta shimbosh ny vooinjerys eddyr daa chretoor nagh vel jeh'n sorçh cheddin. Ta'n askaid freayll y partan sauçhey, as ta'n partan cur yn askaid dys bee noa. Ta'n shimbosh shoh coreggyragh: ta vondeish ec y daa chretoor.” Dooyrt Mabon dy vel y shimbosh coreggyragh myr ny caarjyn echey: ta Mabon mie ec earrooyn, ta Llinos mie ec lhaih, as t'ad ynsaghey y cheilley.

Eisht, hooar Llinos craaish follym jeh partan ayns y gheinnagh, as ny ingnyn echey slane. “Vel y partan marroo?” dooyrt ee. “Cha nel,” dooyrt Delyth. “Ta craaish çhionn mygeayrt corp y phartan, agh cha nel y craaish gaase. Myr shen, tra ta'n partan gaase, t'eh ceau jeh'n craaish shenn, as ta craaish noa bog fo. Ta ny ingnyn echey ayns y craaish shoh neesht.”

Ren ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er y gheinnagh trooid gless mooadaghey. Va dagh grineen anchasley: grineenyn bane, grineenyn doo, as grineenyn beggey jeh shlig. Ec y jerrey, ren Delyth y vrastyl y ghoaill thie roish my daink y keayn erash.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va poyll beg faagit eddyr ny creggyn?
Va'n keayn thannaghey, as va'n ushtey ny s'inshley.
Cre'n cummey t'er corp askaid?
Ta corp rollianagh ec askaid, myr piob veg.
Vel Mabon tushtagh?
Ta. Ta Mabon feer tushtagh, as t'eh shirrey fys mychione dy chooilley nhee.
Cre'n shimbosh honnick ad?
Honnick ad askaid veg er shlig partan, as ta vondeish ec y daa chretoor.
Row'n partan marroo?
Cha row. Va'n partan er ceau jeh'n craaish shenn, as va ny ingnyn echey ayns y craaish.
Cre honnick ny paitçhyn trooid y gless mooadaghey?
Honnick ad grineenyn bane, grineenyn doo as grineenyn jeh shlig.

lessons.title: Yn caffee rish y phurt
lessons.summary: Hafwen Pengilly runs a small café by the harbour in Ramsey and serves the fishermen herself: bacon, toasted bread with butter and an oat porridge, while old Tadhg Furlong puts pepper on everything; when an English visitor asks for pineapple, which is too expensive there, Hafwen offers quince jam from the tree in her garden instead, and everyone is satisfied.
lessons.text:
Ta caffee beg ec Hafwen Pengilly rish y phurt ayns Rhumsaa. T'eh fosley ec shey er y chlag 'sy voghrey, roish my vel ny baatyn goll magh er y keayn. Ta ny eeasteyryn çheet stiagh dy ee as dy iu cappan tey, as ta Hafwen tendeil orroo hene. Cha nel ee laccal sleih elley dy tendeil 'sy chaffee: ta'n obbyr aashagh dy liooar, as ta enney eck er dy chooilley eeasteyr.

Ta'n bee eck mie as çheh. Ta bagoon eck veih eirinagh 'sy glion, as t'ee greddaney arran noa cooyl y chaffee. Ta'n arran greddanit currit er y voayrd lesh eeym bwee veih'n eirinagh cheddin. Ta brod jeh corkey eck neesht, jeant lesh bainney as beggan sollan. “Ta corkey cur niart dhyt son laa liauyr er y keayn,” ta Hafwen gra.

Ta Tadhg Furlong ny eeasteyr shenn, as t'eh çheet dagh moghrey. Ta'n bee cheddin echey dy kinjagh: daa veer jeh bagoon, oohyn, arran greddanit lesh ram eeym, as pibbyr. Ta Tadhg cur pibbyr er dy chooilley nhee: er ny oohyn, er y vagoon, as eer er y brod corkey. “Ta pibbyr jannoo yn bee ny s'çheh,” t'eh gra, “as ta'n keayn feayr.”

Un voghrey 'sy tourey, haink ben noa stiagh. She troailtagh v'ee, veih Sostyn. “Vel annane ayd?” dooyrt ee. “S'mie lhiam annane er arran greddanit.” Va Tadhg gearey. Cha row annane 'sy chaffee rieau. “Ta annane costallagh ayns Rhumsaa,” dooyrt Hafwen, “er-y-fa dy vel eh çheet veih foddey ersooyl. Agh ta quinsh aym.”

Ta billey quinsh ec Hafwen ayns e gharey. Ta ny messyn buigh as creoi, as cha nel ad mie dy ee gyn coagyrey. Ta Hafwen coagyrey ny messyn lesh shugyr, as t'ee jannoo soolagh jiarg jeu. Ren y troailtagh soolagh quinsh y ee er arran greddanit lesh eeym. “Ta shoh ny share na annane!” dooyrt ee. “As cha nel eh costallagh.”

Ec y jerrey, va dy chooilley pheiagh saasit. Va'n troailtagh saasit lesh y quinsh, va Tadhg saasit lesh e vagoon as y pibbyr, as va Hafwen saasit er-y-fa dy row'n caffee lane. Lurg shen, ren Hafwen screeu er y voayrd mooie: “Soolagh quinsh — cha nel eh costallagh.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta tendeil er ny eeasteyryn 'sy chaffee?
Ta Hafwen Pengilly tendeil orroo hene.
Cre ta Hafwen jannoo lesh corkey?
T'ee jannoo brod lesh bainney as beggan sollan.
Cre ta Tadhg cur er dy chooilley nhee?
T'eh cur pibbyr er dy chooilley nhee.
Cre'n fa ta annane costallagh ayns Rhumsaa?
Ta annane costallagh er-y-fa dy vel eh çheet veih foddey ersooyl.
Row'n troailtagh saasit lesh y quinsh?
Va. Va'n troailtagh saasit, as dooyrt ee dy row'n soolagh ny share na annane.

lessons.title: Yn thooilley 'sy glion
lessons.summary: Gruffydd Carveth makes hay in a field by the river for winter fodder and calls his fourteen-year-old daughter Nia lazy because she sleeps late; when the river floods one autumn night, Nia hears a pregnant cow calling, leads it up the hill with a hemp rope, and the next day the calf is born and is spared the slaughterhouse.
lessons.text:
Ta Gruffydd Carveth ny eirinagh ayns glion rish awin. Ta keyrragh echey, kuse dy ollagh, as magher mooar faggys da'n ushtey raad t'eh jannoo traagh dagh sourey. Ta'n traagh tashtit ayns thie mooar cloaie er y chronk, as t'eh ny foddyr son yn ollagh 'sy gheurey. Ta Gruffydd beihll oarn ayns mwyllin veg neesht, as t'eh cur yn oarn vleihit marish y traagh. “Ta'n foddyr share jeant jeh traagh as grine,” t'eh gra.

Ta inneen echey, Nia, kiare bleeaney yeig d'eash. Ta Nia cadley dy liauyr 'sy voghrey, as ta Gruffydd gra dy vel ee litçheragh. “Cha nel mee litçheragh,” ta Nia gra. “Ta mee ynsaghey dy anmagh 'syn oie.”

Un oie 'syn ouyr, haink fliaghey trome. Va'n fliaghey tuittym son daa laa, as dirree yn awin. Ec mean-oie, va'n ushtey harrish y vroogh, as va thooilley ayns y magher. Va booa correy 'sy magher shen, as va'n booa shen er ve correy son bunnys nuy mee.

Cheayll Nia yn booa eam 'sy dorraghys, as roie ee dys shamyr e ayr. “Ta'n ushtey 'sy magher!” dooyrt ee. Hie ad magh lesh soilshey. Va'n booa correy shassoo ayns ushtey derrey e glioonyn. Ghow Nia tead jeh kennip veih'n thie traagh. Ta tead kennip lajer, as cha nel eh brishey ayns ushtey. Ren ee yn tead y chiangley mygeayrt mwannal y vooa, as ren ad y booa y leeideil seose dys y chronk.

'Sy voghrey, va'n thooilley er goll sheese. Va'n traagh 'sy thie er y chronk çhirrym, agh va'n traagh va faagit 'sy magher fliugh. “Cha jean mee ymmyd jeh'n traagh fliugh shen,” dooyrt Gruffydd. “Ta traagh fliugh jeeillagh da'n ollagh: t'eh goll dy olk, as ta traagh olk jeeillagh da ny booa as da ny keyrragh.”

Ayns y fouyir, ta Gruffydd creck dew dys y thie buitçhoorys ayns y valley. Er y laa cheddin, va booa veg ruggit da'n booa correy. Va Nia jeeaghyn er y chretoor beg. “Cha jed ee dys y thie buitçhoorys,” dooyrt ee. “Bee ee freaylt 'sy magher.” Va Gruffydd gearey. “Cha nel inneen litçheragh aym,” dooyrt eh. “Ta inneen aym ta sauail booa 'syn oie.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Gruffydd jannoo lesh y traagh?
T'eh ny foddyr son yn ollagh 'sy gheurey.
Cre ta Gruffydd beihll ayns y vwyllin?
T'eh beihll oarn, as t'eh cur eh marish y traagh.
Cre'n tead ghow Nia veih'n thie traagh?
Ghow ee tead jeh kennip, er-y-fa nagh vel tead kennip brishey ayns ushtey.
Vel Nia litçheragh?
Cha nel. T'ee ynsaghey dy anmagh 'syn oie.
Cre'n fa va'n booa ayns gaue?
Va'n booa correy shassoo ayns ushtey derrey e glioonyn.
Cre'n fa nagh jean Gruffydd ymmyd jeh'n traagh fliugh?
Ta traagh fliugh jeeillagh da'n ollagh.
Jed y booa veg dys y thie buitçhoorys?
Cha jed. Bee ee freaylt 'sy magher.

lessons.title: Yn baatey dragan er y logh
lessons.summary: Eithne Mowat captains a netball team in Ramsey that has been beaten six times this year, so she enters them in the dragon boat race on the lake; the strict coach Rhoswen Guthrie encourages them and allows nobody to speak in the boat except the drummer, and on race day the brave women beat most of the competitors and come second.
lessons.text:
Ta Eithne Mowat ny captan er fwirran lieenvluckan ayns Rhumsaa. Ta shiaght cloiederyn 'sy fwirran lieenvluckan, as t'ad cloie dagh Jeheiney ayns halley y scoill. Agh cha row ad cloie dy mie y vlein shoh. Va'n fwirran bwoailt shey keayrtyn, as va ny cloiederyn trimshagh. “Ta shin bwoailt reesht,” dooyrt Eithne. “Ta feme ain er nhee noa.”

Ta logh mooar ayns Rhumsaa, as dagh sourey ta cohirrey er y logh son baatyn dragan. Ta baatey dragan liauyr as cheyl, as ta kione dragan jiarg er toshiaght y vaatey as famman dragan ec y jerrey. Ta feed sleih ymmyrt 'sy vaatey, as ta un pheiagh soie ec y toshiaght lesh drum mooar. Ta'n peiagh shen bwoalley yn drum, as ta dy chooilley ymmyrtagh goll lesh sheean y drum. “Lhig dooin goll 'sy chohirrey,” dooyrt Eithne. “Ta'n fwirran lieenvluckan ain jeant jeh mraane lajer.”

Ren ad bwoirrin elley y gheddyn, as ren Rhoswen Guthrie, ynseyder spoyrt, ad y ynsaghey. Ta Rhoswen greesee ad dy chooilley laa. Ta Rhoswen neulhoobagh mychione ny reillyn. Ta reill neulhoobagh eck: cha nel peiagh erbee loayrt 'sy vaatey, agh y fer ta bwoalley yn drum. “Ta'n drum ny chree 'sy vaatey,” dooyrt ee. “My ta'n drum tappee, t'ou ymmyrt dy tappee. My ta'n drum moal, t'ou ymmyrt dy moal.”

Er laa y chohirrey, va hoght baatyn dragan er y logh. Va ny cohirreyderyn lajer: va fwirran jeh deiney aile, fwirran jeh eeasteyryn as fwirran veih'n vanc. Va Eithne er y drum. Va aggle urree, agh v'ee creeoil. Ren ee bwoalley yn drum dy lajer as dy kiart, as ren Rhoswen ad y greesee veih'n vroogh: “Ny smoo tappee! T'ou creeoil!”

Ec y toshiaght, va'n baatey oc 'sy queiggoo ynnyd. Eisht, lurg tammylt, ren ad goll shaghey daa vaatey elley. Va ny cohirreyderyn shen ny yei orroo nish. Ec y jerrey, haink ad stiagh 'sy nah ynnyd, ny yei ny deiney aile. Va ny mraane greesit as maynrey.

“Cha nel shin bwoailt jiu,” dooyrt Eithne. “Va shin creeoil, as va'n drum lajer.” Va Rhoswen gearey. “Ta'n reill neulhoobagh mie er y logh,” dooyrt ee. “Er-lhiam dy bee eh mie 'sy lieenvluckan neesht.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va cloiederyn y fwirran lieenvluckan trimshagh?
Va'n fwirran bwoailt shey keayrtyn y vlein shoh.
Cre ta er toshiaght baatey dragan?
Ta kione dragan jiarg er toshiaght y vaatey.
Cre'n reill neulhoobagh t'ec Rhoswen?
Cha nel peiagh erbee loayrt 'sy vaatey, agh y fer ta bwoalley yn drum.
Quoi va ny cohirreyderyn?
Va fwirran jeh deiney aile, fwirran jeh eeasteyryn as fwirran veih'n vanc.
Row ny mraane bwoailt 'sy chohirrey?
Cha row. Haink ad stiagh 'sy nah ynnyd.

lessons.title: Yn turbeen fo'n keayn
lessons.summary: The journalist Clodagh Fyfe interviews Meirion Treganna, a pioneer of sea energy who built the island's first tidal turbine at the mouth of the harbour; he explains that the tide is cyclical and predictable, that the sensors treat the current as a vector, that the water's pressure once broke a blade, and that salt and bromine in seawater damage the metal.
lessons.text:
Ta Clodagh Fyfe ny fysseragh son pabyr-naight ayns Doolish. Un laa 'sy tourey, hie ee dys y phurt dy loayrt rish Meirion Treganna. She jeshaghteyr eh, as t'eh ny noader ayns bree yn keayn. Ren eh as e heshaght yn chied turbeen marrey er yn ellan y hroggal, as ta'n turbeen shen ny lhie fo'n ushtey ec beeal y phurt.

“Cre'n aght ta'n turbeen gobbraghey?” dooyrt Clodagh. Dooyrt Meirion dy vel y turbeen myr mwyllin geayee fo'n ushtey. “Ta'n keayn çheet stiagh as goll magh daa cheayrt 'sy laa,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n gleashaght shoh çhymshallagh: t'eh çheet reesht as reesht, myr ny laghyn as ny bleeantyn. Er-y-fa dy vel eh çhymshallagh, ta fys ain roish laue cre tra vees y stroo lajer, as cre tra vees eh moal. Cha nel shen myr y gheay, nagh vel fys ain er.”

Ta ram glackeyderyn er y turbeen. Ta dagh glackeyder towse yn ushtey: e vieauid, e hroa as e çhiassid. “Ta'n stroo ny vaghtoor,” dooyrt Meirion. “Ta vaghtoor ny nhee lesh mooadys as lesh troa. Cha nel eh dy liooar dy ve fys ain cre cho tappee as ta'n ushtey roie. Ta feme ain er fys c'raad t'eh goll neesht. Ta'n vaghtoor gra dooin cre'n aght dy hyndaa yn turbeen.”

Ta preays mooar er y turbeen. Ta'n ushtey trome, as ta preays yn ushtey er ny skianyn feer lajer tra ta'n stroo ec e niart smoo. Er y chied vlein, ren skian brishey kyndagh rish y preays. Myr shen, ta Meirion as e heshaght aaghlenney y jeshaght dagh blein. “Cha nel jeshaght erbee foddey veih noa,” dooyrt eh. “Ta shin aaghlenney eh lesh dy chooilley nhee ta shin ynsaghey.”

Ta trubbyl elley ayn: ta'n ushtey marrey jannoo jeeill da'n meain. Ta sollan ayns ushtey marrey, as bromeen neesht. “Ta bromeen ayns ushtey marrey er feie ny cruinney,” dooyrt Meirion, “as ta bromeen as sollan cur er y meain goll dy olk.” Er-y-fa shen, ta ny glackeyderyn coodit dy mie.

Ec y jerrey, ren Clodagh feysht y chur: “Vel y turbeen jannoo bree dy liooar?” “Cha nel foast,” dooyrt Meirion. “Ta lectraghys ain son daa cheead thie. Agh ta'n keayn kinjagh çheet, as myr noader, ta mee credjal dy bee ram turbeenyn ayn.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi eh Meirion Treganna?
She jeshaghteyr eh, as t'eh ny noader ayns bree yn keayn.
Cre'n fa ta gleashaght y keayn çhymshallagh?
T'eh çheet stiagh as goll magh daa cheayrt 'sy laa, reesht as reesht.
Cre ta ny glackeyderyn jannoo?
Ta dagh glackeyder towse yn ushtey: e vieauid, e hroa as e çhiassid.
Cre'n fa ren skian brishey?
Ren skian brishey kyndagh rish preays yn ushtey.
Cre ta Meirion as e heshaght jannoo dagh blein?
T'ad aaghlenney y jeshaght lesh dy chooilley nhee t'ad ynsaghey.
Cre ta ayns ushtey marrey marish sollan?
Ta bromeen ayns ushtey marrey.

lessons.title: Yn abb rish yn awin
lessons.summary: The historian Peredur Laing is revising a small guidebook about an old abbey by a river in the south of the island; in the library he reads about the plain monastic life of prayer for salvation and grace, fishing and weaving, a prophet's warning in an old book, and the reformer whose words led to the abbey's closure, and he gets permission to see the old walls.
lessons.text:
Ta Peredur Laing ny shennaghyssagh, as t'eh jannoo aavriwnys er lioar-raad veg mychione abb shenn. Ta'n abb ny lhie rish awin veg 'sy jiass jeh'n ellan, faggys da'n keayn. Va'n chied lioar-raad screeuit roish daeed blein, as ta mynphoyntyn noa er ve feddynit neayr's shen. Myr shen, ta feme er aavriwnys.

Ta Peredur goll dys y lioarlann dagh laa. Ta mynphoyntyn ymmodee ayns ny shenn screeuyn: cre wheesh dy vaynee va cummal 'syn abb, cre va ad dy ee, as cre'n obbyr v'ad jannoo. Va'n vea vaynaghoil cruinn as boght. Ta ny reillyn maynaghoil screeuit ayns lioar veg: shassoo seose roish y ghrian, guee shiaght keayrtyn 'sy laa, as gobbraghey dy chooilley laa. V'ad guee son saualtys nyn anmeenyn, as son grayse Yee. “Cha nel saualtys çheet liorish obbyr,” t'eh screeuit ayns lioar veg, “agh liorish grayse.”

Agh cha row ny maynee guee ny slane laa. V'ad gobbraghey neesht. V'ad goaill eeastyn 'syn awin, as v'ad jannoo fidderaght. Va olley jeh ny keyrragh oc, as va'n fidderaght oc cur sthoo mie as çhiu. Va'n sthoo shen er ny chreck ayns Nerin as ayns Nalbin. Ta Peredur er gheddyn meer beg jeh'n sthoo shen ayns thie-tashtee, as t'eh freayll eh 'sy lioar-raad noa.

Ayns y lioarlann, ren Peredur lioar shenn y gheddyn jeh ny Lioaryn Fadeyragh, screeuit liorish laue maynagh. 'Syn oirr, va'n maynagh er screeu: “Ta'n fadeyr gra dy jig y jerrey.” Ren Peredur eab dy hoiggal shen. Va'n fadeyr feer kiart: haink jerrey yn abb. 'Sy chorrid shey-cheead blein jeig, va aachrootagh ennoil ayns Sostyn. Dooyrt yn aachrootagh shen dy row ny abbyn ro verçhagh, as ren eh loayrt rish y ree. Lurg da'n aachrootagh loayrt rish y ree, va ny shenn abbyn dooint, as va ny maynee ceaut magh. Cha row yn abb rish yn awin ry-hauail.

Jiu, ta'n abb ny ynnyd scanshoil. Ta Peredur laccal fakin cooid jeh ny creggyn fo'n thalloo, agh ta feme echey er lowaltys. Ren eh screeu lettyr dys y reiltys, as lurg mee, hooar eh lowaltys. Ren eh fakin cooid jeh'n voalley shenn, as ren eh ny mynphoyntyn y screeu sheese. Ta'n aavriwnys echey er jerrey nish, as bee'n lioar-raad noa ayns ny shappyn 'sy tourey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Peredur Laing jannoo?
T'eh jannoo aavriwnys er lioar-raad mychione abb shenn.
Cre'n fa va ny maynee guee?
V'ad guee son saualtys nyn anmeenyn, as son grayse Yee.
Cre'n obbyr va ny maynee jannoo marish guee?
V'ad goaill eeastyn 'syn awin, as v'ad jannoo fidderaght.
Cre haink er yn abb lurg da'n aachrootagh loayrt rish y ree?
Va'n abb dooint, as va ny maynee ceaut magh.
Cre va feme er Peredur dy akin ny creggyn fo'n thalloo?
Va feme echey er lowaltys veih'n reiltys.

lessons.title: Yn troddanagh as yn awin
lessons.summary: The activist Tegid Pollard, who once campaigned for gay rights, now campaigns for the river in his glen when the administration proposes a big factory on its bank; the village is divided, he gets a hostile letter, and the hierarchy of offices never answers, so he writes to Lamorna Rintoul, a member of parliament, who proposes building the factory near the harbour instead.
lessons.text:
She troddanagh Tegid Pollard. Roish jeih bleeaney, v'eh gobbraghey myr troddanagh son kiartyn homocheintee, son leigh noa ren yn Ardwhaiyl y ghoaill ec y jerrey. She dooinney homocheintagh eh hene, as t'eh cummal marish e heshey ayns thie beg rish awin ayns glion 'sy twoaie. Nish, t'eh gobbraghey myr troddanagh son yn awin.

Ta'n awin glen as aalin. Ta eeastyn bio ayn, as 'sy tourey ta ny paitçhyn snaue ayn. Agh y vlein shoh, ren y reireydys ayns Doolish skeim noa y hebbal: dy hroggal thie-obbree mooar er broogh yn awin. Dooyrt y reireydys dy beagh obbyr ayn son keead dooinney. Dooyrt Tegid dy jinnagh y thie-obbree jeeill da'n ushtey as da ny eeastyn.

Va meechoardailys mooar 'sy valley. Ren paart jeh ny sleih çheughey rish y reireydys, er-y-fa dy row feme oc er obbyr. Ren sleih elley çheughey rish Tegid, er-y-fa dy row graih oc er yn awin. Va'n meechoardailys cho trome dy row caarjyn shenn gyn loayrt rish y cheilley. Va paart jeh ny sleih noidagh da Tegid hene: un voghrey, va lettyr noidagh fo'n dorrys echey, gyn ennym erbee er. Ren e heshey y lettyr y lhaih, as v'eh trimshagh. “Cha nel ad noidagh dhyt's,” dooyrt eh. “Ta aggle orroo er son nyn obbyr.”

Hie Tegid dys oik y reireydys. Agh ta keimoilaght liauyr ayns y reireydys. Ta'n fer ayns y chied oik screeu da'n fer erskyn eh, as t'eshyn screeu da'n fer erskyn eshyn, as myr shen. Lurg three mee, cha row Tegid er chlashtyn veg. “Cha jig freggyrt erbee trooid y keimoilaght shoh,” dooyrt eh.

Myr shen, ren eh screeu dys Lamorna Rintoul, oltey jeh'n Ardwhaiyl. Haink ish dys y glion, as hie ad cooidjagh rish yn awin. Honnick ee ny eeastyn 'syn ushtey. “Ta mee toiggal y meechoardailys,” dooyrt ee. “Ta feme er obbyr, as ta feme er yn awin neesht. Lhig dou feysht y chur ayns yn Ardwhaiyl.”

Mee ny lurg shen, va arganey ayns yn Ardwhaiyl. Ren Lamorna Rintoul skeim elley y hebbal: dy hroggal y thie-obbree er thalloo follym faggys da'n phurt, foddey veih'n awin. Ren ny olteynyn elley çheughey r'ee. Va'n obbyr ayn foast, as va'n awin sauçhey.

Va'n meechoardailys er jerrey, as va ny caarjyn shenn loayrt reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va Tegid Pollard roish jeih bleeaney?
V'eh gobbraghey myr troddanagh son kiartyn homocheintee.
Cre'n skeim ren y reireydys y hebbal?
Ren y reireydys skeim y hebbal dy hroggal thie-obbree mooar er broogh yn awin.
Cre'n fa ren paart jeh ny sleih çheughey rish y reireydys?
Ren ad çheughey rish y reireydys er-y-fa dy row feme oc er obbyr.
Cre va fo'n dorrys un voghrey?
Va lettyr noidagh fo'n dorrys, gyn ennym erbee er.
Cre'n fa nagh daink freggyrt veih'n reireydys?
Va keimoilaght liauyr ayns y reireydys, as va dagh fer screeu da'n fer erskyn eh.
Quoi ren skeim elley y hebbal ayns yn Ardwhaiyl?
Ren Lamorna Rintoul skeim elley y hebbal: dy hroggal y thie-obbree faggys da'n phurt.

lessons.title: Yn potecaree as ny lioaryn clashtynagh
lessons.summary: Brychan Tresidder, a pharmacist in Peel, brings medicine every Friday to old people who cannot come to his shop; Annwen Polkinghorne, whose illness keeps her at home and whose eyes are too weak to read, listens to an audiobook about a great river in India, remembers the crocodiles and silk cocoons she saw there, and in April walks down to the beach with him.
lessons.text:
She potecaree Brychan Tresidder ayns Pheeil. Ta shapp beg echey rish y phurt, as t'eh creck lheeys as nheeghyn elley son y slaynt. Dagh Jeheiney, ta'n potecaree goll lesh lheeys dys sleih shenn nagh vod çheet dys y shapp.

Ta Annwen Polkinghorne nane jeu. T'ee kiare feed bleeaney d'eash, as ta aslaynt eck. Kyndagh rish yn aslaynt, cha nod ee shooyl foddey, as t'ee tannaghtyn 'sy thie. Agh roish yn aslaynt, v'ee troailt er feie ny cruinney. Va baatey beg eck as ec e sheshey, as dagh sourey v'ad shiaulley er awinyn mooarey ayns çheeraghyn elley.

Un Jeheiney 'sy gheurey, haink Brychan lesh y lheeys. “Kys t'ou jiu?” dooyrt eh. “Ta mee scuirrit,” dooyrt Annwen. “Cha nod mee lhaih nish, er-y-fa nagh vel my hooillyn mie.” “S'treih lhiam clashtyn shen,” dooyrt y potecaree. “Agh ta lioaryn clashtynagh ayns y lioarlann. Ta peiagh lhaih y lioar dhyt, as t'ou eaishtagh rish.”

Er y nah Jeheiney, haink Brychan lesh jeshaght veg. Va lioar chlashtynagh er y jeshaght: skeeal mychione troailt er awin vooar ayns yn Injey. Ren Annwen eaishtagh rish y lioar chlashtynagh dagh fastyr.

Tra haink Brychan reesht, va Annwen maynrey. “Va mee er yn awin shen roish daeed blein!” dooyrt ee. “Ta croggylyn 'syn awin. Un laa, honnick mee croggyl mooar ec y vroogh. Ta sleih gra dy vel y croggyl dewil, agh cha nel eh dewil. T'eh shirrey bee, myr dy chooilley chretoor. Ta sleih ny smoo dewil na croggyl erbee.”

Dooyrt ee neesht dy row ee ayns balley rish yn awin raad ta sleih jannoo sheeidey. “Ta'n praddag jannoo cocoon mygeayrt eh hene,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n cocoon jeant jeh snaie feer veen. Ta ny sleih goaill y snaie veih'n chocoon, as t'ad jannoo sheeidey jeh.”

Eisht va Annwen gearey. “Ta mee myr praddag ayns cocoon nish,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mee ayns my hie beg ny slane gheurey. Agh 'sy arragh, hig mee magh, as hed mee sheese dys y traie.”

'Sy vee Averil, va Annwen ny share. Hie ee sheese dys y traie marish y potecaree, as honnick ee ny baatyn 'sy phurt.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n potecaree jannoo dagh Jeheiney?
T'eh goll lesh lheeys dys sleih shenn nagh vod çheet dys y shapp.
Cre'n fa nagh vod Annwen shooyl foddey?
Cha nod ee shooyl foddey kyndagh rish yn aslaynt eck.
Cre dooyrt y potecaree tra nagh dod Annwen lhaih?
Dooyrt eh: “S'treih lhiam clashtyn shen.” Eisht haink eh lesh lioar chlashtynagh.
Cre'n fa nagh vel y croggyl dewil, rere Annwen?
T'eh shirrey bee, myr dy chooilley chretoor.
Cre ta'n praddag jannoo mygeayrt eh hene?
T'eh jannoo cocoon jeh snaie feer veen.
Cre ren Annwen 'sy vee Averil?
Hie ee sheese dys y traie marish y potecaree.

lessons.title: Yn lhong-aer fo'n ushtey
lessons.summary: A small syndicate of five divers in Port St Mary looks for a wartime plane from a squadron that fell into the sea in 1943; with everything prepared and permission from the government, Kerra Kittow finds the wreck on the third day and, in the pilot's cabin, a tin box holding a lucky coin with the name of Sergeant Fearghas Moodie, which they give to his grandson.
lessons.text:
Ta syndacait beg ayns Purt Çhiarn. Ta queig thummeyderyn 'sy syndacait, as ta baatey oc cooidjagh. Ren dagh oltey jeh'n syndacait eeck son ayrn jeh'n vaatey, as t'ad goll magh er y keayn dagh Jesarn 'sy tourey. Ta Kerra Kittow ny captan, as ta Dughall Baillie ny shennaghyssagh.

Ta Dughall er ve lhaih mychione y Nah Chaggey Mooar. Ayns 1943, va squadroon jeh lhongyn-aer cummal ayns Mannin. Va'n squadroon shen freayll arrey er ny lhongyn er y keayn. Un oie 'sy gheurey, haink trubbyl er lhong-aer jeh'n squadroon, as ren ee tuittym 'sy keayn faggys da Purt Çhiarn. Va daa ghooinney er boayrd: y stiureyder, as sarjant aeg, Fearghas Moodie. Ren baatey eeastee ad y hauail, agh cha row y lhong-aer rieau feddynit.

Hooar Dughall caslys shenn ayns y thie-tashtee, as va'n ynnyd er y chaslys raad ren y lhong-aer tuittym. “Lhig dooin shirrey ee,” dooyrt eh rish y syndacait. Ren eh screeu dys y reiltys, as hooar eh lowaltys dy ghoaill nheeghyn veih'n lhong-aer.

Ren ad y baatey y chiartaghey. Va dy chooilley nhee kiartit: va ny tankyn aer lane, va ny teadyn er boayrd, as va'n caslys kiartit lesh ny earrooyn noa. Er y chied laa, cha dooar ad veg. Er y nah laa, cha dooar ad veg. Er y trass laa, hie Kerra sheese, as honnick ee skian 'sy gheinnagh. V'ee er gheddyn y lhong-aer!

Va'n lhong-aer ny lhie er y gheinnagh fo'n ushtey, as va lus marrey er dy chooilley ayrn jee. Va dorrys yn cabbane foshlit. She cabbane beg v'ayn, raad va'n stiureyder soie. Hie Kerra stiagh dy moal. Ayns yn cabbane, hooar ee kishtey beg stainney. Va'n stainney doo, agh va'n kishtey slane.

Er y vaatey, ren ad y kishtey stainney y osley. Va cooiney ayn, as va ennym y harjant screeuit er y chooiney. “She cooiney son aigh t'ayn,” dooyrt Dughall. “Va cooiney son aigh ec ram sleih 'sy chaggey.”

Ren ad shirrey mychione y sarjant. Hooar Fearghas Moodie baase roish feed blein, agh ta mac e vac cummal ayns Sostyn. Haink eshyn dys Purt Çhiarn, as hug Kerra y kishtey stainney da, lesh y cooiney 'sy chishtey. “Va my hennayr kinjagh loayrt mychione y cooiney shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Dooyrt eh dy row y cooiney er hauail e vea.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta 'sy syndacait ayns Purt Çhiarn?
Ta queig thummeyderyn 'sy syndacait, as ta baatey oc cooidjagh.
Cre va'n squadroon jannoo ayns y chaggey?
Va'n squadroon freayll arrey er ny lhongyn er y keayn.
Quoi va er boayrd y lhong-aer?
Va'n stiureyder as sarjant aeg, Fearghas Moodie, er boayrd.
Cre va kiartit er y vaatey?
Va ny tankyn aer lane, va ny teadyn er boayrd, as va'n caslys kiartit.
Cre hooar Kerra ayns yn cabbane?
Hooar ee kishtey beg stainney ayns yn cabbane.
Cre va 'sy chishtey stainney?
Va cooiney ayn, as va ennym y harjant screeuit er.
